title: Frontend: Kruskal's MST Algorithm
businessContext: Build and verify the core behavior behind Kruskal's MST Algorithm. This independently authored exercise has a bounded, explicit contract. Injected clock, network, random, or worker models are identified in the contract; they do not claim production service guarantees.
problemStatement: Implement solution({count,edges}). Return {weight,components} for the minimum spanning forest of an undirected weighted graph using Kruskal and disjoint-set union. Self-loops are ignored. Parallel/negative edges are supported; empty graph has zero components.
constraints: Define solution(input) in plain JavaScript. Return the documented JSON-compatible value or throw the documented validation error. Each case receives a fresh input.
Preserve identity, ordering, boundary behavior, and error messages stated in the contract. Passing fixtures verifies this contract, not every production concern.
candidateTasks: Implement the documented behavior without hard-coding fixture answers.
Run the full suite, investigate boundary failures, and explain the follow-up variation.
hints: Write down the state or algorithmic invariant, and trace the smallest boundary case before coding.
Sort undirected edges by weight, then use a disjoint-set union structure with path compression and union by rank/size.
alternativeApproaches: Return component information and a deterministic tie-breaking policy without claiming the MST is unique.
commonMistakes: Ignoring contract boundaries such as: Cycle edge rejected; disconnected graph; negative weights.
Treating a local deterministic model as proof of durable storage, authorization, distributed coordination, or physical-world guarantees.
